scope: Frozen DATA-007 lifecycle maintenance trust boundary
Compiler-generated persistence create and retention-purge boundaries
Validated environment binding in maintenance and first-party initialization
Focused lifecycle runtime regressions and supplied validation report

trustBoundary.assumption: The frozen contract makes lifecycle maintenance compiler-owned and non-source-callable. A trusted host starts the generated worker; Jadpo source, public routes, service keys, principals, and authored callables cannot mint or invoke its maintenance capability (docs/lifecycle-plan.md:159-167).
trustBoundary.implementation: configureLifecycleRetention is a named generated-module export imported by generated host integration as bindLifecycleRetention (jadpo/crates/core/src/target.rs:846-854); it is not a method on the exported persistence client (target.rs:5715-5722). The binding is reached by generated maintenance and initializeApplication host paths. Treating arbitrary trusted-host module consumers as adversaries would be a different threat model; under the frozen source/public-route boundary this is not a finding.

findings.result: The persistence create boundary recomputes compiler-owned initial values, rejects conflicting caller-supplied values, and persists the computed values. Direct-boundary regressions cover forged User and Todo state and confirm no row is stored.

The purge method accepts no caller cutoff. It fails closed without a captured operation time or initialized retention, and computes eligibility from the bound duration and min(operationTime, Date.now()), preventing future-time cutoff forgery.

Retention is no longer captured from Bun.env at module import. The maintenance entry binds its loaded configuration; initializeApplication binds the environment it validates after authentication initialization succeeds. The mismatch regression confirms the configured five-day duration controls purging even when Bun.env says thirty days.
